did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Jehoshaphat died, his son Jehoram succeeded him as king, and Jehoshaphat was buried in the City of David.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat gave his other sons many gifts—silver, gold, treasures, and fortified cities in Judah—but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
Did you know? After Jehoram had established himself as king, he killed all his brothers with the sword, as well as some of the officials of Israel.
Did you know? Scripture connects Jehoram’s evil ways with the influence of the house of Ahab, because his wife was Ahab’s daughter.

Did you know? Although Jehoram did evil in the eyes of the Lord, the Lord did not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with David and his promise to leave him and his descendants a lamp for all generations.
Did you know? During Jehoram’s reign, Edom rebelled against Judah’s rule and appointed a king of its own.

Did you know? After Edom rebelled, Libnah also revolted. Scripture explains this by saying that Jehoram had abandoned the Lord, the God of his ancestors; during that time, he also built high places and led Judah astray.
Did you know? The prophet Elijah sent Jehoram a letter rebuking him for not following the ways of Jehoshaphat and Asa, and for killing his brothers, who were better than he was.

Did you know? The Lord stirred up the Philistines and the Arabs against Judah. They invaded the land and carried away the possessions of the king’s palace, along with his sons and wives; only Jehoahaz, his youngest son, was left.

Did you know? Jehoram died after suffering a severe and prolonged illness of the intestines. The people did not honor him with a funeral fire like the one held for his ancestors. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
